newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power investing S$1 bln in 5-yrs in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power investing S$1 bln in 5-yrs in Asia.

text.p: Singapore Power Chairman Ho Kwon Ping said on Wednesday the company will invest about Singapore $1.0 billion mainly in the Asia Pacific region over the next five years.

"Singapore Power, through its wholly owned subsidiary Singapore Power International will set aside about S$1.0 billion for overseas investment over the next five years, that is about S$200 million annually from 1997 to 2001," Ho said in an interview with Reuters.
"We are currently looking into opportunities in China, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, India and Australia," he said.
These investments could be in new projects or acquiring an equity interest in existing generation and distribution companies, he said.
Ho said the electricity industry in Singapore is a maturing one with growth estimated at 7.0 percent annually.
"However, demand for electricity in the Asia Pacific region is projected to grow very substantially, especially in developing and newly industrialised member economies," he said.
